# FigJam Board Design

> FigJam's own palette with one meaning per colour, one pink first glance and Inter at seven sizes. Flat, light and drawn on an 8 pixel grid.

This file is the style every board `assets/compose-board.js` draws. Change a token in the json block in Section 8 and every board composed after it follows. Nothing else needs editing. `scripts/compose_board.py` reads the block, sends the composer only the tokens that differ from its built-in design and names every token it could not use.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

A board is drawn from FigJam's own palette, so anyone on it can recolour a node from FigJam's picker later. A design never adds a colour. It chooses which FigJam pair carries which meaning.

Three layers carry a colour from this file to a node:

- **Swatches** are FigJam's own pairs, each a fill, a stroke and a text colour, and its light section tints. The block lists them as reference, and they stay as FigJam ships them
- **Roles** say what a colour means, such as `goal` or `decision`, and each names one swatch. This is the layer a team restyles
- **Kinds** are what a model draws, such as a decision or a data store. Each kind names one role and the words its key entry shows, and its shape stays the composer's

So `"goal": "lightTeal"` turns every goal on every board teal and the key says so, while the shapes, the layout and the routing stay as they are. The board is flat: no shadow, no gradient and no fill on the board itself beyond white.

---

## 2. COLOUR ROLES

| Role | Swatch | What it marks | Drawn by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entry` | Light blue | Where a reader starts | A flow's start, a state diagram's first state |
| `neutral` | White | An ordinary step | Screens, steps, states, services, sub-processes, entities, participants and planned bars |
| `goal` | Light green | The outcome the flow exists for | A flow's goal |
| `exit` | Light orange | A way out of the flow | An exit end |
| `error` | Light red | An error or a block | An error end, a critical gantt bar |
| `decision` | Light yellow | A choice, or a point a plan reaches | Decisions, state choices, milestones |
| `store` | Light violet | Data at rest | Data stores |
| `io` | Light teal | Input or output | Input and output steps |
| `client` | Light teal | An app or a client | Architecture clients |
| `gateway` | Light blue | The edge of a system | Architecture gateways |
| `queue` | Light orange | A queue or a stream | Architecture queues |
| `external` | Light gray | A system outside the board's scope | Architecture outside systems |
| `inProgress` | Light blue | Work under way | Gantt bars in progress |
| `done` | Light gray | Work finished | Gantt done bars, a state diagram's final states |
| `pseudo` | Charcoal | A state machine's own marks | Start and end dots, fork and join bars |
| `junction` | Dark gray | Paths that join | A flow's merge dot |
| `marker` | Violet | A numbered pin | A sequence's step numbers |

Light blue serves three roles but never two on one board. A flow and a state diagram start in it, an architecture marks its gateways in it and a gantt chart its work in progress, and the key names the one a board uses. Light teal, light orange and light gray split the same way, by diagram type.

---

## 3. THE ACCENT

The accent marks the one node, message or task a reader should see first. It is a pair no role draws, light pink by default, drawn as an `accent.node` outline of 8 pixels around a node or bar and an `accent.message` line of 4 pixels along a sequence message. A user flow or a process names it with a `style` line and the other types with `%% focus:`, as `references/style-guide.md` Section 3 sets out.

It keeps first place by three measures, which Section 7 holds every edit to:

- Its stroke clears 3:1 on white
- Its hue sits 45 degrees or more from every role a kind draws, every tint in the zone cycle and every line colour and the key's tint
- Its outline outweighs every other mark: heavier than the 6 pixel ring of an end state on a node, and heavier than the lines on a message

---

## 4. KINDS AND THE KEY

Each kind in the `kind` group names its role and its key words. `focus` names no role, because it draws the accent's own pair. The key shows one sample per kind, line and arrow the board draws, the kinds in the composer's own order, which reordering the `kind` group does not change, then the lines, the arrows, the step pin and the focus last. It is as wide as the diagram, and an entry that would run past that edge starts a new row.

The `key` group holds the key's own words: its title, the step pin's entry and one entry per line style and sequence arrow. Its `tint` is the section tint the key sits on.

---

## 5. TYPE

| Token | Default | Weight | Where it is used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | 64 | Bold | The board's title |
| `subtitle` | 28 | Regular | The line under the title, wrapped between 960 and 1440 pixels into even lines |
| `zone` | 24 | Semi Bold | Zone names and the key's title |
| `node` | 20 | Medium | Node labels and entity names |
| `label` | 18 | Medium on a connector, Regular elsewhere | Edge labels, key entries, gantt axis and task names, the source line |
| `field` | 16 | Regular | Entity fields |
| `small` | 14 | Medium | Gantt bar lengths and step pins |

`family` names the face. The board loads its Medium, Regular, Semi Bold and Bold styles, taking Semi Bold under either name FigJam gives it, `Semi Bold` or `SemiBold`. When a style will not load, the board is set in Inter and the composer's warnings say so, so pick a family that carries all four.

---

## 6. LINES AND ZONES

| Token | Default | Draws |
|---|---|---|
| `line.color` | `#757575` | Every connector, and a sequence's requests and replies |
| `line.async` | `#3DADFF` | A sequence's async messages and replies |
| `line.lifeline` | `#B3B3B3` | A sequence's lifelines |
| `line.weight` | 2 | Every line but the accent's |

A line colour is one of the colours the swatch block holds, any fill, stroke or text, so it stays on FigJam's palette.

`zone.cycle` lists the section tints zones and gantt sections take in turn. Each takes the first tint along the cycle that no node inside it draws and that no zone beside it took, within two zone gaps on any side. An orange exit never sits in an orange zone and two neighbouring zones never read as one, however the layout placed them. When no tint keeps both rules, a zone keeps the neighbour rule, repeats a member's hue and the composer's warnings say so. Pink stays out of the cycle, because it is the accent's hue, and gray is left for the key.

Spacing stays the composer's: the gaps between ranks and zones, the zone margins and the board's margin. The router measures every clearance against that spacing, so a board that reads cramped is fixed in the model, as `references/style-guide.md` Section 7 sets out.

---

## 7. FLOORS

A token that misses a floor falls back to its built-in value and the rest of the design stands. When the file changed two tokens that miss a floor together, one falls back at a time and the floors are measured again, so the other stands once the floor holds.

| Floor | Measure |
|---|---|
| Text on a fill | Each role's text colour on its fill at 4.5:1 or more |
| The accent's own pair | No role names the accent's pair |
| The accent's hue | 45 degrees or more from every saturated role stroke, zone tint, line colour and the key's tint on the board |
| The accent's contrast | Its stroke at 3:1 or more on white |
| The accent's weight | A node outline over 6 and up to 16 pixels, a message line heavier than the lines and up to 8 |
| Lines | 1 to 4 pixels, `line.color` at 3:1 or more on white and `line.async` and `line.lifeline` at 2:1 or more, because an open head also marks an async message and a lifeline is a guide |
| Dots | A start, an end, a merge and a fork carry no label, so the fill of the role each draws measures 3:1 or more on white |
| Kinds apart | No two kinds one type draws share a shape, a pair and an outline |
| Type | `small` 14 or more, `label` and `field` from `small` up to `node`, `node` 16 to 24, `zone` from `node` up to 24, the largest zone name the router keeps a zone's head clear for, `subtitle` from `zone` up to `title`, `title` from twice `node` up to 128 |
| Names | A role or the accent names a swatch, a kind names a role, the cycle and the key's tint name section tints, the cycle holds two or more tints once each and never the key's tint |
| Words | Key words and `meta.name` on one line of 40 characters or fewer, every character of them text |

Three more rules keep a bad edit from passing silently:

- A group or a token the composer does not read is left out, and a value of the wrong type falls back
- An edit to a swatch or a tint is ignored, because those are FigJam's own colours
- A file with no json block, two blocks, a block that does not parse or another `schemaVersion` falls back whole to the built-in design, and so does one the reader cannot handle for any other reason, so an edit never stops a board

Do pick a role's swatch for what it means on every board, and keep the accent the only pink. Do not give two kinds of one type the same swatch and shape, and do not reach for a colour outside FigJam's pairs, because a custom colour drops out of FigJam's picker.

---

# Example - User Flow - Fernhouse Return

Fernhouse is a fictional store used across the Product Owner fixtures. Every name, screen and rule here is invented for the example.

---

## 1. REQUEST

```text
$flow how a customer starts a return in the app, from these screenshots and the returns doc
```

Sources: five app screenshots and a returns doc.

| Source | Says |
|---|---|
| `Orders - Tap_ Order row.png` | The order list, a row under the finger |
| `Order detail - Tap_ Start a return.png` | The order page with a Start a return button |
| `Return reason - Select_ Reason.png` | A list of reasons |
| `Return method - Select_ Drop-off or pickup.png` | Two choices: a drop-off point or a courier pickup |
| `Return confirmed.png` | A confirmation with a QR code |
| Returns doc, Section 2 | Returns are open for 30 days after delivery. After that the app shows Contact support. Current behavior |
| Returns doc, Section 4 | A free pickup for orders over €100. Proposal, under review |

---

## 2. TYPE AND DIALS

- **Reader question:** which screens does a customer pass through to start a return, and where do they choose? A user flow
- **Detail:** balanced. **Audience:** mixed, so the labels use the app's own words
- **Look:** left to right in three zones, finding the order, requesting the return and done. The confirmation is styled as the goal, so the main line runs from the order list to it and Contact support sits below as an exit

---

## 3. PLAYBACK

The playback is its own reply, sent before the model. It waits for its own answer, and a yes to it moves the work on to the model and writes nothing.

```text
Before I draw anything, this is how I read the request.
Question: which screens does a customer pass through to start a return, and where do they choose?
Outcome: a reader can follow a return from the order list to a confirmed return and see where the 30 day window ends it.
Settled by the sources: the five screenshots give the screens and the returns doc, Section 2, gives the 30 day window and its Contact support exit.
Left out: the free pickup over €100, a proposal under review in Section 4 of the returns doc.
Assumed: balanced detail and a mixed audience, so the labels use the app's own words.
Still open: none.
Is this the right reading of the board?
```

---

## 4. MODEL

The first draft, kept as text because it fails the check:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    orders([Order list]) --> detail[Order detail]
```

15	# FigJam Hybrid Workflow
16	
17	A model cannot put a note on a step. The composer draws everything else a model carries: the title, the zones, the colour of every kind, the sequence's step numbers and the key. So the hybrid workflow adds one thing, notes, with `use_figma` inside the board the write returned. Every note is a new node on top of the board. A composed node is never moved, resized or restyled.
18	
19	**Loading Condition:** ON_DEMAND, when the request asks for notes, callouts or data on specific nodes that the model cannot carry
20	**Purpose:** When to add notes to a composed board, the two recipes, their gate and their rollback, and how a board of several diagrams is planned
21	**Scope:** Additions through `use_figma` on the composed route. The generated and `fj` routes add nothing beyond the diagram
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 1. WHEN TO EXTEND
26	
27	Notes cost a second write, a read of the board and a wider rollback, so they are a judgement, not a default.
28	
29	Extend when:
30	
31	- The request asks for something the model cannot carry: notes, callouts or the reason behind a step
32	- The sources hold data that belongs on specific nodes, such as a drop-off rate, an owner or a service level
33	- The board is for others, such as a team review, and three or more nodes need a note
34	
35	Do not extend when:
36	
37	- The request is short and plain, such as "draw the checkout states"
38	- The diagram has under 8 nodes and a note would be louder than the diagram
39	- The ask is colour, grouping, a title, numbering or a key. The composer draws each of those from the model, so the fix is a model change, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 5 sets out
40	
41	Figma ranks the value by type. Annotation helps a flowchart most, and sequence, state and gantt notes are added only when asked for.

46	
47	1. **Compose** the board and keep the `fileKey` and the board id the write returned. Send the URL to the user as soon as it lands, before extending

51

54	Every node inside a zone has coordinates relative to that zone, so a recipe places a note from the target's `absoluteBoundingBox` minus the board's, never from the `x` and `y` a read reports.

title: "FigJam Hybrid Workflow"
description: "How to add notes the model cannot carry to a composed FigJam board: numbered pins with a sticky legend or a single sticky, each additive, gated and reversible, plus how a board of several diagrams is planned."
contextType: implementation
importance_tier: important
trigger_phrases:

  - "annotate figjam diagram"
  - "sticky legend"
  - "numbered pins"
  - "use_figma extension"
version: 1.0.1.0
---

# FigJam Hybrid Workflow

A model cannot put a note on a step. The composer draws everything else a model carries: the title, the zones, the colour of every kind, the sequence's step numbers and the key. So the hybrid workflow adds one thing, notes, with `use_figma` inside the board the write returned. Every note is a new node on top of the board. A composed node is never moved, resized or restyled.

**Loading Condition:** ON_DEMAND, when the request asks for notes, callouts or data on specific nodes that the model cannot carry
**Purpose:** When to add notes to a composed board, the two recipes, their gate and their rollback, and how a board of several diagrams is planned
**Scope:** Additions through `use_figma` on the composed route. The generated and `fj` routes add nothing beyond the diagram

---

## 1. WHEN TO EXTEND

Notes cost a second write, a read of the board and a wider rollback, so they are a judgement, not a default.

Extend when:

- The request asks for something the model cannot carry: notes, callouts or the reason behind a step
- The sources hold data that belongs on specific nodes, such as a drop-off rate, an owner or a service level
- The board is for others, such as a team review, and three or more nodes need a note

Do not extend when:

- The request is short and plain, such as "draw the checkout states"
- The diagram has under 8 nodes and a note would be louder than the diagram
- The ask is colour, grouping, a title, numbering or a key. The composer draws each of those from the model, so the fix is a model change, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 5 sets out

Figma ranks the value by type. Annotation helps a flowchart most, and sequence, state and gantt notes are added only when asked for.

---

## 2. THE PATTERN

1. **Compose** the board and keep the `fileKey` and the board id the write returned. Send the URL to the user as soon as it lands, before extending
2. **Pick** the target nodes by their ids in the write's node list, which carries each node's model id and label, or from a `get_figjam` read in a later session
3. **Extend** with one `use_figma` call on the same `fileKey`, following one recipe below, and return every created id with the board's size before the call
4. **Read back** the notes, as Section 6 sets out, and reply

Never create a new file and never call `figma.createPage()`, which throws on a FigJam file. Write `use_figma` code as plain JavaScript with top-level `await` and a `return` of every created id, as Figma's `figma-use` skill requires, and load a node's font before setting its text.

Every node inside a zone has coordinates relative to that zone, so a recipe places a note from the target's `absoluteBoundingBox` minus the board's, never from the `x` and `y` a read reports.

---

## 3. RECIPES

### Numbered pins with a sticky legend

The default for three or more notes. A small numbered circle sits on each annotated node's top-left corner, and the matching stickies stand in a column inside the board, to the right of the diagram, each starting with its number. The write widens the board to hold the column. The diagram stays clean and ten notes read as easily as three. The column stands 200 pixels clear of the diagram, a same-topic gap, and its stickies keep FigJam's 64 pixel grid between rows, as `style-guide.md` Section 7 sets the bands.

```javascript
const before = { w: board.width, h: board.height }
const origin = board.absoluteBoundingBox
const probe = figma.createSticky()
await Promise.all([figma.loadFontAsync(probe.text.fontName), figma.loadFontAsync({ family: 'Inter', style: 'Medium' })])
probe.remove()
const created = []
const edge = board.width - 80
let top = Infinity
for (let i = 0; i < notes.length; i++) {
  const box = (await figma.getNodeByIdAsync(notes[i].id)).absoluteBoundingBox
  const pin = figma.createShapeWithText()
  pin.shapeType = 'ELLIPSE'
  pin.name = `pin:${i + 1}`
  pin.text.fontName = { family: 'Inter', style: 'Medium' }
  pin.text.characters = String(i + 1)
  pin.text.fontSize = 20
  pin.resize(48, 48)
  pin.fills = [{ type: 'SOLID', color: h('#874FFF') }]
  pin.strokes = [{ type: 'SOLID', color: h('#5427B4') }]
  pin.text.fills = [{ type: 'SOLID', color: h('#FFFFFF') }]
  board.appendChild(pin)
  pin.x = box.x - origin.x - 24
  pin.y = box.y - origin.y - 24
  top = Math.min(top, pin.y)
  created.push(pin.id)
}
let y = top
let right = edge
for (let i = 0; i < notes.length; i++) {
  const sticky = figma.createSticky()
  sticky.name = `note:${i + 1}`
  sticky.text.characters = `${i + 1}. ${notes[i].note}`
  sticky.fills = [{ type: 'SOLID', color: h('#A8DAFF') }]
  board.appendChild(sticky)
  sticky.x = edge + 200
  sticky.y = y
  y += sticky.height + 64
  right = Math.max(right, sticky.x + sticky.width)
  created.push(sticky.id)
}
```

- The violet pin is the one preset whose white digit clears the text gate, as `style-guide.md` records. A sequence already numbers its messages with smaller pins in the `marker` role, so a note on a sequence names its message number in the sticky rather than adding a second pin beside it

### A single sticky

For one or two notes, a sticky beside its node is clearer than a legend, so a request for one or two notes gets this form and no pin, no legend column and no sticky at the board's far edge. Place it inside the board, to the right of the node, or above or below when the right is taken, 64 pixels clear, which is the gap a sticky keeps from the sticky beside it, and widen the board when the sticky reaches past its margin. Name it `note:<n>`, so the read-back counts it by name. Past two notes, switch to pins and a legend. Never mix the two in one diagram.

---

## 4. WHAT AN EXTENSION NEVER DOES

- Moves, resizes, rewires or restyles a composed node. A layout that reads badly is fixed in the model and composed again
- Draws a node, a connector, a zone, a title or a key entry. Each of those belongs in the model, so the composer draws it and the read-back counts it
- Writes outside the board section the write returned, or to a file other than the one the gate named, or creates a page
- Uses a colour outside `style-guide.md`. A brand colour asked for by name is a hand edit, and the reply says it is off-palette
- Adds what nobody asked for. Every unrequested sticky is noise

The notes sit inside the tagged board section, so a later session that finds the board by its tag finds its notes with it, and replacing the board replaces them too.

---

## 5. GATE AND ROLLBACK

The yes before the first write covers the notes only when the gate message named them: what will be added, on which nodes, and that the rollback deletes the ids the extension returns. Notes decided after the board landed need their own yes.

The rollback is to delete exactly the ids the extension returned and resize the board to the size the extension returned as `boardBefore`, through `use_figma`, after a yes to the deletion. Stop when an id is gone or belongs to a node that is not a pin or a note inside this board.

---

## 6. READ-BACK

Read the board with `get_figjam` and count the pins and the notes by name against what the extension planned, then check one screenshot for a pin or a sticky that covers a label. The line takes the form the recipe drew, pins with a legend or single stickies.

```text
Extensions: 4 of 4 pins, 4 of 4 legend stickies, 0 overlaps
Extensions: 2 of 2 notes, 0 overlaps
```

The first line is for three or more notes drawn as pins with a legend. The second is for one or two notes drawn as single stickies. The line sits after the board's own `Read-back:` line in the reply.

---

## 7. WHEN AN EXTENSION FAILS

The board already landed and the user already has its URL. Report what landed and what did not, with the error in a few words. When `use_figma` reports `safeToRetryWithoutCanvasRead: true`, fix the error and retry once. Otherwise read the board, find what the failed call left, and ask before deleting any of it.

---

## 8. A BOARD OF SEVERAL DIAGRAMS

Work that needs two or more diagrams is planned before the first write, so a reader knows where one ends and the next begins and where to start.

- Each diagram is its own composed board, with its own title, key and tag, in the one file this work writes
- The title carries the diagram's ordinal and then its name, such as `%% title: 2. Workspace setup`, so the boards read as one numbered set
- The composer places each new board 400 pixels to the right of everything already on the page, its top level with the highest node, so the boards read left to right in the order they were written. Write them in reading order, because no later call moves one
- A split flow ends one board on a named hand-off node and starts the next board from the same name, so the reader follows the hand-off from one board to the next
- The reply names the board a reader opens first, by its ordinal and its name, and that first board is the one the reader's question starts in
